title: Taifa of Silves
capsule: The Taifa of Silves was an Arab Muslim principality based at Silves (Shilb) in the Algarve region of southwestern Iberia, ruled by the Banu Muzayn from around 1027 following the fragmentation of the Umayyad Caliphate of Córdoba. The city commanded the Arade River valley and was a notable centre of Andalusian poetry, most famously associated with the eleventh-century poet Ibn Ammar, vizier to the emir al-Mutamid of Seville. Silves was absorbed by the Almoravid empire around 1063 and briefly reasserted independence as a second taifa from 1145 before the Almohad Caliphate extinguished it definitively in 1150. Portuguese forces captured the town in 1189 and, after a Moorish reoccupation, permanently in 1242.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The taifa's political history is documented in Arabic chronicles and later Portuguese sources, but precise territorial control beyond the Silves hinterland is not well mapped.
